# Move workers from config.yaml to Compose


iii 0.23 removes the old worker lifecycle. There is no compatibility period and no automatic
migration. These are gone: the `iii worker` command, the `worker::*` functions, worker lookup
through `iii.toml`, and project workers declared in `config.yaml`.

Each project now declares its project workers in the `containers:` section of `worker-compose.yaml`.
When Compose starts the engine, the optional `engine:` section configures it. If `config.yaml` still
declares a project worker, engine startup and config reload stop with `UNSUPPORTED_CONFIG_WORKERS`.
The error lists every entry to migrate.

## Replace `iii worker` and `worker::*` calls

Each removed `worker::*` function has a `compose::*` replacement, except `worker::clear` and
`worker::logs`:

| Removed function   | Replacement                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `worker::add`      | `compose::add`                                                                       |
| `worker::remove`   | `compose::remove`                                                                    |
| `worker::update`   | `compose::update`                                                                    |
| `worker::start`    | `compose::up`                                                                        |
| `worker::stop`     | `compose::down`                                                                      |
| `worker::list`     | `compose::status`                                                                    |
| `worker::status`   | `compose::status`                                                                    |
| `worker::schema`   | `compose::schema`                                                                    |
| `worker::validate` | `compose::validate`                                                                  |
| `worker::logs`     | No direct replacement. `compose::logs` returns recent output of the project workers. |
| `worker::clear`    | No replacement.                                                                      |

Replace each `iii worker` command with the matching `iii trigger compose::*` call, for example
`iii trigger compose::add worker=http`.

## Hand the migration to a coding agent

The steps below are mechanical, so a coding agent with shell access to the project can carry them
out. Copy this prompt into the agent, then review the resulting `worker-compose.yaml` before
starting it.

```text Prompt wrap
Migrate this iii project from config.yaml worker declarations to worker-compose.yaml (iii 0.23). Read https://iii.dev/docs/upgrading/workers-to-compose.md first and follow it exactly.

Before changing anything:
1. Locate every config.yaml (including any path passed with --config), any existing worker-compose.yaml, iii.lock, the configuration worker's storage directory (./config by default), and the state, queue, and stream data paths. Copy all of them into ./backup-pre-compose/, preserving each source's relative path so two files with the same name never collide, and stop if a destination already exists. Do not delete the originals.
2. Make sure no other supervisor, for example systemd or Kubernetes, runs this project. If the repository does not make this clear, ask me before you write the file.

Write worker-compose.yaml:
- Move configuration, iii-worker-manager, iii-http-functions, iii-stream, and iii-sandbox into the engine.workers map. The map value is the worker config itself; drop the old nested config: key. Multiple instances use a #instance suffix.
- Do not declare iii-engine-functions, iii-telemetry, or iii-observability. The engine injects them.
- Move every other worker under containers:. Rename it per the table on the page (iii-state or state becomes state, iii-http or http becomes http, and so on). Registry workers use package://api.workers.iii.dev/<name> with an explicit version; local workers use path://. Set config_name to the container key for each package container. If config.yaml still has a config: block for a worker, copy it to config_override. Keep every storage path unchanged.
- Translate each iii-exec entry into scripts. Join every exec command except the last into scripts.pre_run with &&, and put the last command in scripts.run. Wrap each command in parentheses before you join them with &&.
- Pin versions from iii.lock or the registry. Never invent a version number.
- For a separately supervised engine, keep only the five engine-owned workers in the list-shaped config.yaml and omit engine: from the Compose file.

Stored configuration: after a worker's first boot, 0.22 moved its config: block into the configuration worker under the worker's config.yaml name, such as iii-state. For each project worker, read the stored value with configuration::get and raw: true, so any ${VAR} templates stay as templates. Read each value before you upgrade, while the 0.22 engine runs. If 0.23 is already installed, read the value field of ./config/<id>.yaml in ./backup-pre-compose/. When config_name equals the 0.22 name, such as state, the worker reads the stored value as it is; skip that worker. Copy the value to the container's config_override. Replace each secret in the copied value with a ${VAR} reference before you write the file. Verify the new worker before you remove the old entry. Do not rename YAML files as a shortcut.

Never edit the generated engine-config.yaml in the Compose state directory.

Stop after you write worker-compose.yaml. Show me the file and wait for my approval. After I approve, start the project. If III_URL is set in the shell, unset it before you start a managed engine. iii compose stays in the foreground, so run it in a second terminal or send it to the background with its output in a log file, then wait until it has started every container:
  iii compose --up --file worker-compose.yaml
  (for a separately supervised engine: start the engine with iii --config config.yaml under its own supervisor, then iii compose --engine <that engine's ws:// URL> --up --file worker-compose.yaml)

With the daemon running, show me the output of:
  iii trigger compose::status file=worker-compose.yaml
  iii trigger engine::workers::list
  iii trigger engine::triggers::list
Run these commands from the project directory. iii trigger reads engine.url from worker-compose.yaml there. If the engine runs at another address, add --engine ws://<host>:<port> to each iii trigger command.

If startup reports UNSUPPORTED_CONFIG_WORKERS, UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE_WORKER, ENGINE_WORKER_IS_INJECTED, or any other error from the Common errors list on the page, fix the cause and rerun. Do not work around an error by deleting a worker.

Report back: the resolved path and diff of every configuration file you changed, including any passed with --config, the full new worker-compose.yaml, which stored configuration ids you migrated, and anything you could not migrate.
```

## Back up the project

Keep a copy of:

- `config.yaml` and any path passed with `--config`
- an existing `worker-compose.yaml`
- the configuration worker's storage directory, `./config/` by default
- state, queue, and stream data paths
- `iii.lock`, if `iii worker add` created one

The 0.23 engine does not accept the old project-worker declarations. To roll back, restore these
files and install the previous engine version:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.iii.dev/iii/main/install.sh | sh -s -- <previous-version>
```

For a release candidate, also give `--rc`. See
[Install a pre-release](../install#install-a-pre-release).

## Preserve stored configuration

In 0.22, each project worker kept its settings in the configuration worker under its `config.yaml`
name, such as `iii-state` or `state`. Under Compose, a worker reads the id in its `config_name`. The
sample in [Move project workers to containers](#move-project-workers-to-containers) sets
`config_name: state`, so that worker reads `state`. When `config_name` equals the 0.22 name, as with
`state`, the worker reads the stored value as it is. Skip steps 1 to 4 for that worker, and keep its
entry. Without `config_name`, the id is `<namespace>-<container-key>`, for example `default-state`.
Compose does not copy a value from an `iii-` id. For the naming rules, see
[Readable configuration names and migration](../using-iii/compose#readable-configuration-names-and-migration).

1. Before you upgrade, read each old value with any `${VAR}` templates intact:

   ```bash
   iii trigger configuration::get id=iii-state raw=true
   ```

2. Copy the returned `value` to the container's `config_override`. 0.22 expanded `${VAR}` references
   before it stored the block, so the copied value can hold secrets as plain text. In
   `config_override`, replace each secret with a `${VAR}` reference.
3. After you start the project, verify the new worker.
4. Remove the old entry. With the default `fs` adapter, delete `./config/iii-state.yaml`.

Do not only rename the YAML file. Each file also holds the entry id and metadata.

`iii-stream` keeps its settings in the stored `iii-stream` entry, and its `engine.workers` value
only seeds an empty store. To change a stored setting, use `configuration::set`. See
[Two configuration layers](../using-iii/configuration#two-configuration-layers).

## Build the new engine section

Move the configs of the five engine-owned workers from list entries in `config.yaml` to the
`engine.workers` map: `configuration`, `iii-worker-manager`, `iii-http-functions`, `iii-stream`, and
`iii-sandbox`. For the field reference, see [Engine fields](../using-iii/compose#engine-fields).

The map value is the worker config itself; do not keep the old nested `config:` key. Multiple
instances use a `#instance` suffix, such as `iii-worker-manager#rbac`.

```yaml worker-compose.yaml
engine:
  url: ws://127.0.0.1:49134
  workers:
    configuration:
      adapter:
        name: fs
        config:
          directory: ./config
    iii-worker-manager:
      host: 127.0.0.1
      port: 49134
    iii-http-functions: {}
    iii-stream:
      host: 127.0.0.1
      port: 3112
    iii-sandbox:
      auto_install: true
```

`engine.url` defaults to `ws://127.0.0.1:49134`. If you omit `iii-worker-manager`, Compose sets its
host and port from `engine.url`. If you declare it, its `port` must match the port in `engine.url`.
A declared entry with no `port` uses 49134. If the ports differ, startup fails with
`MANAGED_ENGINE_ENDPOINT_MISMATCH`.

Compose generates the engine configuration from this section. Do not edit the generated file. For
its location, see [Where compose keeps state](../using-iii/compose#where-compose-keeps-state).

Remove explicit `iii-engine-functions`, `iii-telemetry`, and `iii-observability` entries. The engine
injects them. An entry under `engine.workers` fails with `ENGINE_WORKER_IS_INJECTED`. An entry in
`config.yaml` fails with `UNSUPPORTED_CONFIG_WORKERS`.

## Move project workers to containers

| Old name                 | Compose package                   |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `iii-http` or `http`     | `http`                            |
| `iii-cron` or `cron`     | `cron`                            |
| `iii-queue` or `queue`   | `queue`                           |
| `iii-state` or `state`   | `state`                           |
| `iii-pubsub` or `pubsub` | `pubsub`                          |
| `iii-bridge`             | `bridge`                          |
| `iii-exec`               | no package; use Compose `scripts` |

Copy the current settings of each project worker to its `config_override`. On first boot, 0.22 moved
each `config:` block from `config.yaml` into the configuration worker and left a comment in its
place. Read the current value as [Preserve stored configuration](#preserve-stored-configuration)
shows. Also copy any `config:` block that is still in `config.yaml`. Keep every storage path. A
package worker runs in the directory that holds `worker-compose.yaml`, so its relative paths resolve
there. Run `iii compose` from that directory, so the `configuration` worker finds `./config` in the
same place. Pin each package version.

```yaml worker-compose.yaml
containers:
  state:
    worker: package://api.workers.iii.dev/state
    version: "0.22.2"
    config_name: state
    config_override:
      adapter:
        name: kv
        config:
          store_method: file_based
          file_path: ./data/state_store.db
  http:
    worker: package://api.workers.iii.dev/http
    version: "0.21.3"
    config_name: http
    config_override:
      host: 127.0.0.1
      port: 3111
  app:
    worker: path://.
    start_after: [state, http]
    scripts:
      pre_run: pnpm build
      run: pnpm start
      post_run: pnpm cleanup
```

Translate each `iii-exec` entry into `scripts`. `iii-exec` ran its `exec` commands in order and kept
the last one running. Join every command except the last into `pre_run` with `&&`. Put each command
in parentheses, for example `(cd frontend && npm install) && (cd frontend && npm run build)`.
`iii-exec` ran each command in its own shell, so a `cd` in one command did not change the next one.
Put the last command in `run`. `pre_run` has a default budget of 60 seconds. Set `pre_run_timeout`
for a longer build. Compose has no `watch` setting. After you change the code, run
`iii trigger compose::restart container=app`. Compose waits until each container registers a worker
with the same name as its container key. With iii-sdk 0.23 or later, the worker uses
`III_WORKER_NAME`, which Compose sets to the container key. A worker on an older SDK that sets its
own name fails with `WORKER_NAME_MISMATCH`. Upgrade its SDK. A command that does not connect to iii
fails with `STARTUP_TIMEOUT`. Custom local workers use `path://`. Registry workers use `package://`
and a version.

To add another registry worker while Compose runs, use `compose::add`. It writes the worker under
`containers:` with the resolved version. It starts the new worker and restarts only the containers
whose declaration changed. It does not change `engine:`.

```bash
iii trigger compose::add worker=cron
```

If the registry lists the worker with kind `engine`, the `compose::add` operation fails with
`ENGINE_WORKER_IS_BUILTIN`. For one of the five engine-owned workers, the error names the
`engine.workers` key to use. To see the error, run
`iii trigger compose::operation operation_id=<operation_id>`.

## Start the result

When the file has an `engine:` section, Compose starts the engine and the project workers:

```bash
iii compose --up --file worker-compose.yaml
```

If `III_URL` is set in your shell, Compose connects to that address and does not start an engine.
Unset `III_URL` before you run this command.

Without `--namespace`, Compose uses the `namespace:` value of the file, or `default` when the file
has none. In `default`, project workers behave as in 0.22, and callers reach their functions with no
namespace. If the daemon runs in another namespace, add `-n <namespace>` to each
`iii trigger compose::*` command. To move a project to another namespace, set `namespace:` in the
file and follow Steps 1, 4, and 5 of [Upgrading from 0.22.x to 0.23.x](./from-0-22-x).

Changing `engine:` while the daemon runs returns `ENGINE_RESTART_REQUIRED`. Stop and restart that
Compose invocation. A second file with `engine:` returns `ENGINE_ALREADY_OWNED`.

For an engine supervised separately by systemd or Kubernetes, keep its five engine-owned workers in
the list-shaped `config.yaml`, start it directly, omit `engine:` from the Compose file, and supply
the existing URL:

```bash
iii --config config.yaml
iii compose --engine ws://127.0.0.1:49134 --up --file worker-compose.yaml
```

Run those commands under separate supervisors. Compose uses the first engine address that it finds
in this order: `--engine`, the `III_URL` environment variable, `engine.url` in the Compose file, and
then `ws://127.0.0.1:49134`. For details, see
[Which engine Compose uses](../using-iii/compose#which-engine-compose-uses).

Verify the migration:

```bash
iii trigger compose::status file=worker-compose.yaml
iii trigger engine::workers::list
iii trigger engine::triggers::list
```

In the `compose::status` output, each entry in `containers` shows `"state": "ready"`.
`engine::workers::list` shows each container key as a worker name. `engine::triggers::list` shows
the trigger types of the new workers, such as `http`, `cron`, and `state`.

## Common errors

- `UNSUPPORTED_CONFIG_WORKERS`: `config.yaml` declares a worker other than the five engine-owned
  workers. Move each project worker to `containers:` in `worker-compose.yaml`. Remove each worker
  that the engine injects.
- `UNSUPPORTED_ENGINE_WORKER`: `engine.workers` contains a project or unknown worker.
- `ENGINE_WORKER_IS_INJECTED`: remove an automatically supplied internal worker.
- `ENGINE_RESTART_REQUIRED`: restart Compose to apply a changed engine section.
- `ENGINE_ALREADY_OWNED`: start the second file with an `engine:` section in a separate Compose
  invocation.
- `ENGINE_SECTION_REQUIRES_MANAGED_START`: a Compose daemon that uses an external engine was asked
  to load a file with an `engine:` section.
- `ENGINE_WORKER_IS_BUILTIN`: `compose::add` was given a registry package of kind `engine`.
- `CONTAINER_NAME_TAKEN`: another live process owns the same `(namespace, worker name)`.
